messages:
rebecca: FYI getting a steady stream of latency complaints from 03:40 UTC onward. p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms -> ~1s, p99 up to 3.8s. several customers opened tickets with traces attached. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/overview?from=now-2h

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-58 (severity: P1) by rebecca. Pager duty: oncall-eng paged.

tom: grabbing traces now. are these all on the new driver/firmware wave? I remember a GPU firmware push last night.

jess: confirmed pattern across eu-central-1 and us-east-1. No big RPS increase. Tail latencies align with hosts that received GPU firmware v2.4.1 and NVMe firmware 1.9.0-rc.

owen: quick host check (i-0f1e2d): top shows inference workers blocked in io wait (wa ~ 20-30%). iostat -x shows svctm & await jumping; avgqu-sz spikes to >200 during tails. dmesg: repeated "nvme0: namespace timeout" and a handful of "nvidia_uvm: DMA timeout" logs.

jess: interesting - GPU firmware having DMA timeouts hints at driver/firmware interaction causing stalled DMA ops, which backpressure NVMe IO. could be path where model runtime does big GPU->host transfers that get serialized.

rebecca: customers reporting 504s from the API gateway when compute stage hits long tails. we need short-term mitigation to reduce customer impact, and a reproduction + root cause plan.

deploy-bot: Noted: small runtime change (prefetch throttle) deployed 08:17 UTC yesterday to reduce prefetching; change flagged as low-risk.

tom: mitigation idea set 1 (network/route): 1) divert heavy tail customers to a hot spare dedicated pool (pool-dedicated-1) with older firmware. 2) lower concurrency per worker from 8 -> 4 to reduce overlapping DMA bursts.

jess: mitigation idea set 2 (host-level): 1) disable NVMe APST on affected nodes (APST sometimes induces latency when devices switch pstates) with `nvme set-feature -f 0x0c -v 0` (check device support), 2) temporarily set scheduler to noop and increase nr_requests to 1024.

own: running a short fio on affected instance to characterize device tails:
```
fio --name=tail-check --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --runtime=30 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1
read: IOPS=52k, lat (usec): p50=180, p95=6200, p99=55000
```

rebecca: those p99s match customer traces. Good reproduction. Please also collect nvme-cli logs (`nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`) and `nvme get-log` to capture transit latency counters.

jess: I ran a narrow experiment on a canary: rebooted GPU with older firmware (v2.3.7) on one host while leaving NVMe firmware. After that, inference tail drops dramatically (fio p99 down to ~9ms). That suggests GPU firmware change is a big factor.

own: rolling a quick traffic shift: diverting 40% traffic away from upgraded pool to dedicated older-firmware pool. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift job 86042 started: 40% -> pool-dedicated-1.

(rebecca 5m later): partial relief seen: customers on diverted pool show baseline latencies. remaining hosts still taily. Need to choose whether to rollback GPU firmware or apply host-level IO tunings at scale.

tom: rollback path for GPU firmware has risk (driver compatibility, node reboots). Host-level tuning is less disruptive: plan to disable APST, set scheduler noop, bump nr_requests, and temporarily disable async io batching in runtime. If that holds for 2 hours, keep firmware and open a firmware/driver escalation with vendor.

jess: how to disable APST quickly across a host fleet (playbook):
1) verify APST supported: `nvme get-feature -f 0x0c /dev/nvme0n1`
2) disable: `nvme set-feature -f 0x0c -v 0 /dev/nvme0n1`
3) verify state with `nvme get-log -i 0x0c`
Also note some vendors require firmware workarounds; check NVMe vendor doc.

own: started a mass-run of noop scheduler + nr_requests=1024 via orchestration on 8 hosts. Quick local fio shows p99 improved from 55ms -> 8-12ms.

rebecca: good. next: ops should run a battery of tests on one fully-upgraded host:
- fio random read/write with qdepth sweep (1,4,16,64)
- nvme smart-log and nvme-cli vendor logs
- check dmesg for nvidia_uvm and nvme errors after synthetic workload
- run a short inference tail harness (our synthetic generator with 1k short requests and 50% cache miss)
Include commands in casebook.

jess: reproduction steps for runbook (copyable):
1) ssh to upgraded host (HOST=x.x.x.x)\2) `sudo fio --name=tail-check --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --runtime=60 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --direct=1`\3) `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1`\4) `sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep "nvme|nvidia_uvm"`\5) run local inference harness: `./tools/synth-infer --model /models/resnet --concurrency 6 --batch-size 8 --requests 1000`

own: adding quick fix: disabled APST on 8 hosts and toggled scheduler to noop. Observed p99 drop to near baseline in those hosts. Rolling to remaining upgraded hosts now (ETA 18m).

rebecca: customer comms: inform impacted customers we've put mitigations in place (traffic diversion + host IO tuning). We're working on root cause with vendor.

jess: postmortem asks: capture exact GPU firmware versions, NVMe firmware, kernel version, driver stack (CUDA + nvidia driver), and runtime changes. Also capture workload telemetry: avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, and number of simultaneous DMA transfers per worker.

tom: long-term actions proposed:
- add a synthetic combined GPU+NVMe tail test to canary pipeline (fio + short inference tails)
- include NVMe APST and vendor-specific features in our preflight checklist for firmware upgrades
- limit runtime prefetch concurrency until we have verified firmware combos

deploy-bot: Run summary logged to INC-2026-58.

rebecca: current status: mitigations deployed to all affected upgraded hosts (IO tuning + scheduler), traffic still 40% on dedicated older-firmware pool until we validate for 2 hours. Keeping incident open. I'll update on progress in 30m. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
